checks: Verified the byte digest for b0296f8a3b0d3d48 and checked §2 equations (3)–(5). The frozen proof establishes the source's surface and cone relations using only positivity at the face and apex.

Affine positivity at the apex and face gives positivity on their entire compact convex hull. The equation N·v=HL(v)>0 on the face proves N is nonzero and puts the image plane at distance H/|N| from the transformed apex. No positivity of the scalar s alone is needed.

Differentiating along an orthonormal tangent frame gives the stated columns. Appending v'=v/L removes all derivative terms proportional to v'. The remaining determinant is H L^(−d). Since the normal component of the last column is H/|N|, the tangential Jacobian is |N|L^(−d). In dimension one the determinant of the one radial column gives the counting-measure Jacobian one.

The explicit inverse is well-defined on the image since its denominator is L(0)/L(v)>0. Reweighting the segment coefficients by L maps each segment onto the segment of the images, so the image is precisely the compact convex pyramid over the transformed face.

Area change cancels the factor |N|L^(−d) to give the constant H/|N| times transformed intrinsic area. On a measurable image patch, a non-apex point has a unique radial coordinate because N·v'=H. The radial determinant contributes t^(d−1)H/|N|, whose integral in t is H/(d|N|). The apex has zero d-volume, so this works for arbitrary measurable patches.
